When to Use What? (Decision Guide)

✅ 1. LRU (Least Recently Used) ⭐
✅ Use when:

You want to keep recently accessed data
Access pattern is temporal (recent = important)
General-purpose systems


✅ Real Examples:

Web apps (user profile, product pages)
OS page replacement
Redis default


✅ Why?
👉 Recently used data is likely to be used again

✅ Rule:
👉 If unsure → use LRU

✅ 2. LFU (Least Frequently Used)
✅ Use when:

Some data is accessed very frequently
You want to keep hot data


✅ Real Examples:

Trending products
Popular videos
Frequently accessed configs


✅ Why?
👉 High-frequency data should stay longer

✅ Rule:
👉 Use LFU when access pattern = frequency-based

✅ 3. FIFO (First In First Out)
✅ Use when:

Simple system
Order matters more than access pattern


✅ Real Examples:

Queue-like systems
Logs (oldest removed first)


❌ Avoid when:

Access pattern matters


✅ Rule:
👉 Use FIFO for simple, predictable systems

✅ 4. TTL (Time-To-Live) ⭐ MUST KNOW
✅ Use when:

Data becomes stale after time
Need automatic expiry


✅ Real Examples:

Sessions (login tokens)
API responses
Cache with freshness requirement


✅ Why?
👉 Ensures data is always fresh

✅ Rule:
👉 Use TTL for time-sensitive data

✅ 5. MRU (Most Recently Used)
✅ Use when:

Recently used data is less likely to be reused


✅ Rare Example:

Sequential data access patterns


❌ Not common in real systems

✅ Rule:
👉 Rarely used — only for special workloads

✅ 6. Random Eviction
✅ Use when:

Need very fast eviction
Complexity should be minimal


✅ Real Examples:

Some distributed systems
When performance > accuracy


❌ Risk:

May remove important data


✅ Rule:
👉 Use when speed matters more than precision

🔥 ✅ Quick Decision Cheat Sheet
General use → LRU ✅
Hot data (frequently used) → LFU ✅
Time-based expiry → TTL ✅
Simple system → FIFO
Very fast + simple → Random
Rare special case → MRU


✅ ✅ Interview Answer (Perfect)

“LRU is used for general-purpose caching where recent data is more valuable. 
LFU is used when frequently 
accessed data needs to be retained. TTL-based eviction is used for time-sensitive data 
to ensure freshness. FIFO is used in simpler systems, while MRU and random 
eviction are used in specific or performance-critical scenarios.”
